checks.name: no_kappa_bar_in_contributions
checks.evidence:
Contributions block (section1_introduction_draft.tex:26-29) verified. Full text:
  \item A two-layer constrained decoding framework, motivated by a decidability analysis establishing that IE type constraints require runtime state beyond CFG expressiveness (Proposition~1), yielding pair-based sequential enforcement at each level (§sec:decidability). Constraints compile automatically from IE ontologies, validated on schemas of varying restrictiveness with up to 96 relation types.
  \item A comprehensive evaluation of type constraint enforcement across 3 IE datasets, 4 models (7--70B), and 2 tasks: (a) for RE, the five-way ablation confirms that neither layer alone achieves >24% DR reduction while their composition yields 94--100%, and that fine-tuning does not obviate constraints (residual DR 1--2% at R-F1 40--46%); (b) preliminary event extraction results on WikiEvents demonstrate generalization to 245 constraints across three tokenizer families (§sec:wikievents).
No \bar{\kappa}, no '94-99%', no '42-90%'. κ̄ detail replaced with 'schemas of varying restrictiveness'.
